data.name: Calebian
data.long_meaning: The name Calebian is derived from the Hebrew word 'kalev' meaning 'tend, cultivate, keep, observe'. It is often used as a reference to the biblical figure Caleb, who was a descendant of Jacob and one of the original twelve spies sent by Moses to explore the Promised Land. Caleb, also known as Calib with God, was one of the few spies who had faith in God's promise to give the Israelites the land, and as a result, he was granted the land he explored as his inheritance. Therefore, the name Calebian can be understood as a name for someone who follows and tends to God's word and promises.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name for someone who is faithful and follows God's promises.

data.cultural_impact: The name Calebian can be seen as a testament to the faith and courage of the biblical character Caleb, who trusted in God's promise even when it seemed unlikely. It can serve as a reminder of the importance of staying strong in one's beliefs and holding onto hope, even in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Calebian carries a deep spiritual significance as it represents a connection to the biblical figure Caleb and the values he embodied, such as faith, courage, and obedience to God's will. It can serve as a reminder to stay steadfast in one's spiritual journey and to trust in God's promises, even when they may seem unreachable or uncertain. Additionally, the name can serve as a reminder to tend to one's spiritual growth and cultivate a deep connection with God, just as Caleb tended to the land he was given as his inheritance.

historical_references.reference: In the Old Testament book of Joshua, the Israelites under the leadership of Joshua conquer the Promised Land and divide it among the twelve tribes. One of the territories allotted to the tribe of Judah was named after Caleb, a faithful servant of Moses who had previously spied out the land. (Joshua 14:6-14)
historical_references.context: Biblical account of the conquest of Canaan and the division of the Promised Land among the tribes of Israel

historical_references.reference: Caleb is also mentioned in the New Testament book of Hebrews as one of the old testament believers who did not doubt God's promise and received a reward: 'But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land into which he went; and his seed shall possess it.' (Hebrews 11:13-14)
historical_references.context: New Testament recognition of the faith of Caleb
